Brazil 1822–2026: who ruled, what was handed over, and what happened to wages and wealth

One shared year axis for every term of power, every transfer case, and the data on public patrimony, purchasing power, concentration and democracy. Built from the data files by build_timeline.py.

What the timeline shows

Transfers cluster in a few periods, and each period has a different mix of democracy, wages and inequality. These are patterns in time, not proof of motive.

  1. Military rule, 1964–1985: democracy scores at their lowest (V-Dem 0.144–0.290), state-company investment at its peak (6.54% of GDP in 1976), and the real minimum wage falling from R$ 1,353 (1964) to R$ 789 (1984).
  2. The 1990s sales: 25 cases start in 1995–1999 and yearly privatization money peaks at US$ 37.5 bn in 1998, under high democracy scores (V-Dem 0.849 in 1998). The real minimum wage was R$ 613 (1995) and R$ 688 (1999), the Gini stayed near 61.4, and net public debt rose from 30.0% (1994) to 59.9% of GDP (2002).
  3. 2003–2014: the survey Gini fell from 59.6 to 52.6 and the minimum wage rose to R$ 1,403, while the top 1% kept 27.3–32.7% of national income.
  4. 2016–2021: 27 cases start, V-Dem drops from 0.861 (2015) to 0.699 (2020), and net debt rises to 61.4% of GDP (2020).
Correlation, not proof. Lines moving together in the same years do not show that one caused the other, or why anyone acted. Old eras also have thinner records: 109 of 186 cases start in 1990 or later.

What deals did each president sign, and what followed?

Each row is a signed deal. 'Followed by' shows disasters later tied to that deal. A link is not proof of cause; read the chain.

158 deals over 165 rows (a deal with signing acts in two terms is listed under each, with that year). 15 long processes are listed as "ongoing under" their start term. 15 disasters are tied to a deal from their "linked transfer" text. Who got and who paid show the first sentence of the case; hover for the full text. Deaths are added up only where the data gives a number.

acted = a source names the person acting in the case. in office at the time = held the post; no source names them acting. Each figure keeps its status pill.

How deals were placed, and what was left out
  • Term: the term in office on the signing date when the case text gives a full date in its start year and several terms held office that year; otherwise the term the case sits under below. Later signing acts in another term come from the case's own text.
  • Not deals (left out): e2-16: the state created its own companies (public sector got the assets); e3-02: pollution costs of a state-led pole; no one was handed an asset (who got: not applicable); e4-03: tally of the PND sales, already listed one by one; e6-21: the Union's attempt to win back voting power after a sale; x-01: cost estimates for the Zona Franca, listed under e3-07; x-03: estimate of the scale of land-grabbing, not one act; x-19: yearly series of tax expenditures, not one act; e6-28: yearly total of tax expenditures, not one act.
  • Listed once: x-06 is listed under e3-11; x-10 is listed under e4-13; x-13 is listed under e4-17; x-20 is listed under e5-13; x-23 is listed under e5-14.
  • Disaster links: each disaster's "linked transfer" text was matched to case titles by word overlap, year and exact date, with a short hand-checked list for the rest. Disasters dated before their deal are shown but not counted.
  • Disasters with a linked-transfer text but no deal here: Hydro Alunorte red-mud / bauxite waste overflow, Barcarena: the text names a 2011 sale between two private firms, which is not a case; Amapá blackout: the 2008 LMTE transmission concession is not a case; North and Northeast blackout (Belo Monte transmission): the text names the 2014 transmission auction, not the dam concession (e5-15); Chevron Frade field oil leak: the text says the concession round was not identified; Munduruku standoff against the Teles Pires and Sao Manoel dams: no case matched the text; UHE Estreito hydroelectric dam: no case matched the text; Barra Grande dam: environmental study that hid araucaria forest: no case matched the text.

Notes on every series drawn (27), with the method notes as the researchers wrote them
  • verified Public investment, whole public sector (general government + federal SOEs), % of GDP (% of GDP) FGV IBRE Observatorio de Politica Fiscal, Investimentos Publicos serie historica 1947-2025
    Read from the FGV IBRE Observatorio de Politica Fiscal xlsx 'investimentos_publicos_1947-2025.xlsx' (opened via Wayback copy http://web.archive.org/web/20260521133228id_/https://observatorio-politica-fiscal.ibre.fgv.br/sites/observatorio-politica-fiscal.ibre.fgv.br/files/u49/investimentos_publicos_1947-2025.xlsx; the live site was in maintenance). Per FGV the series splices IBGE Seculo XX, Gobetti (2006) and Orair (2016), then STN from 2011 and SEST from 2015. Values copied as in the file, no interpolation. Column 'setor publico' (SP). Flow of investment, not a stock of capital.
  • verified Investment of federal state-owned enterprises (EPU), % of GDP (% of GDP) FGV IBRE Observatorio de Politica Fiscal, Investimentos Publicos serie historica 1947-2025
    Read from the FGV IBRE Observatorio de Politica Fiscal xlsx 'investimentos_publicos_1947-2025.xlsx' (opened via Wayback copy http://web.archive.org/web/20260521133228id_/https://observatorio-politica-fiscal.ibre.fgv.br/sites/observatorio-politica-fiscal.ibre.fgv.br/files/u49/investimentos_publicos_1947-2025.xlsx; the live site was in maintenance). Per FGV the series splices IBGE Seculo XX, Gobetti (2006) and Orair (2016), then STN from 2011 and SEST from 2015. Values copied as in the file, no interpolation. Column 'empresas publicas' (EPU). SOE investment only; falls after privatizations (Telebras, Vale) as those firms leave the perimeter, see Orair TD 2215 footnote 9.
  • verified Privatization result per year, federal + state programmes (sale receipts + debt transferred), 1991-2002 (US$ bn (nominal)) MDIC/BNDES, Privatizacao no Brasil 1990-1994, 1995-2002, Resultados Acumulados (updated 26 Aug 2002), "Evolucao Anual" chart
    Bar labels read from page 3 of the opened PDF and mapped to years by x-position of the axis labels (2.0=1991, 3.4=1992, 4.2=1993, 2.3=1994, 1.6=1995, 6.5=1996, 27.7=1997, 37.5=1998, 4.5=1999, 10.7=2000, 2.9=2001, 2.0=2002). Labels are rounded; they sum to 105.3, matching the report's total of US$105.298 bn (87.222 receipts + 18.076 transferred debt). Replaces the Social Watch 1997-2002 series (privatization-proceeds-annual-usd), which has the same shape but different values (26.3, 35.7, 4.2, 10.2, 2.8, 2.0). 2002 is partial (report dated Aug 2002). 1990 is not shown separately in the chart.
  • unverified Number of federal state-owned enterprises, DEST series (1980-2011) (count) DEST/MPOG slide "Evolucao do Numero de Empresas" in Henriques, Aula 5 (ENAP), p.13
    Bar-chart labels read on the opened slide (1980=215, 1990=186, 2000=103, 2010=124, 2011=128); the slide's 2011 breakdown table also sums to 128. Counting base is the DEST/SEST universe of the Programa de Dispendios Globais and is NOT the same as the broader 'active under Sest coordination' count of the 2021-22 boletins (federal-soe-count-sest-active-2021-2022) nor comparable without caution to federal-soe-count (2003-2017). The slide is a government training deck (secondary compilation of DEST data).
  • unverified Federal SOEs controlled directly or indirectly by the Union, early 1995 (count) Ipea, Aspectos do Financiamento das Empresas Estatais no Brasil (1995), citing SEST
    Text in the opened PDF: 'De acordo com informacoes da SEST, existem atualmente 149 empresas controladas direta ou indiretamente pela Uniao.' Dated by publication year 1995 (the same paragraph gives balance data as of 31.12.1993). Citation of SEST by Ipea, not the SEST dataset itself.
  • verified Number of federal state-owned companies (EEF, Sest registry) (companies) Ipea, A Configuração das Empresas Estatais Federais: evolução de 2003 a 2017 (BAPI n.15, 2018), citing Boletim das Empresas Estatais/Sest
    Only years stated in the paper text (2003=131, 2006=140, 2016=151, 2017=147; also 2000-02 average ~110, not included as a year). Includes dependent firms, financial institutions and subsidiaries per Sest registry; other Sest/DIEESE sources give different totals for 2017-2019 (138-149; 200 in DIEESE 2021) because of counting criteria. Pre-2000 series not found.
  • verified Federal SOEs active under Sest coordination (quarterly boletim) (count) Boletim das Empresas Estatais Federais (Sest/ME), editions 19 (3T21), 21 (1T22), 23 (3T22)
    Sentences read in the opened boletins: 3T21 'total de 158 empresas estatais federais ativas' (ed. 19); 1T22 '155 empresas' (ed. 21, .../arquivos/21o-boletim-das-empresas-estatais-federais-1t22.pdf), not plotted; 3T22 '130 empresas' (ed. 23). One point per year kept (2021 = 3T21, 2022 = 3T22). Counting base includes subsidiaries, so it is much larger than the directly controlled / investment-budget counts (about 42-47); do not splice with federal-soe-count (2003-2017).
  • verified Federal government internal debt, % of GDP (historical) (% of GDP) IPEADATA HIST_DTGFN (IBGE Anuário Estatístico apud Abreu 1992; Ferreira, Política monetária e dívida pública)
    Gross internal federal debt, 1909-1969; series marked INATIVA by IPEA; compiled from several authors, not comparable to DLSP above (gross, federal only).
  • verified Public sector net debt (DLSP), % of GDP, year-end (% of GDP) Banco Central do Brasil, Notas Econômico-financeiras (Finanças Públicas), via IPEADATA series PAN_DTSPY
    Net debt (liabilities minus financial assets) of the consolidated public sector; says nothing about non-financial assets (land, companies). Methodology revisions by BCB over time. Monthly BCB SGS 4513 (api.bcb.gov.br) matches from 2001 (e.g. Dec 2001 = 51.49).
  • verified Real monthly minimum wage (R$ of Sep 2026 per month) IPEA Data GAC12_SALMINRE12 (Salario minimo real), from MTE nominal minimum wage
    Yearly mean of 12 monthly values, full years 1941-2025 only (1940 and 2026 partial, omitted). Constant R$ of the last month in the series (Sep 2026). IPEA deflators: IPC-SP/Fipe Jul/1940-Jan/1944, IPC-RJ/FGV Jan/1944-Jan/1948, IGPC-Mtb Jan/1948-Mar/1979, INPC Apr/1979 onward; July 1994 deflator step adjusted x1.2225 for currency change. Before May 1984 there were regional minimums: series uses the highest in force. Does not include abonos.
  • verified Mean household income per capita, all sources (PNAD / PNAD Continua, harmonised) (R$ of 2025 per month) IPEA Data PNADS_RENDAMEDIA (after Souza & Hecksher 2025; IBGE PNAD and PNAD Continua)
    Monthly household per-capita income of all sources at last-year prices (2025). Old PNAD (to 2011) multiplied by IPEA factor that equates old PNAD to PNAD Continua in 2012. No survey in 2000 and 2010 (census years) so those years are absent; nothing interpolated. Starts 1995 in this IPEA series (older PNAD years 1976-1994 not found in downloadable form).
  • verified Real GDP per capita, long run (Maddison) (2011 US$ (international, PPP-adjusted)) Maddison Project Database 2023, sheet Full data, country BRA
    Values as published (sheet "Full data", gdppc), 1900-2022, no interpolation. Real GDP per capita in 2011 US$. Ref page: https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/historicaldevelopment/maddison/releases/maddison-project-database-2023. Pre-1900 values exist but are cut for this chart.
  • verified Income inequality (Gini, 0-100) of household income per person, PNAD/PNAD Continua, 1995-2025 (Gini index (0-100)) IPEADATA series PNADS_GINI (Souza & Hecksher 2025 harmonisation of PNAD and PNAD Continua)
    Downloaded via IPEA OData API (ValoresSerie PNADS_GINI), updated 2026-05-25. Household per-capita income, all sources, survey data (no tax data). Pre-2012 old-PNAD values are multiplied by the factor that equates old PNAD with PNAD Continua in 2012, so the series is harmonised. No survey in 2000 and 2010. Surveys under-capture top incomes, so Gini is lower than tax-adjusted estimates.
  • verified Income inequality (Gini, 0-1) of household income per person, old PNAD, 1976-2014 (Gini index (0-1)) IPEADATA series PGINI (Gini, Pnad/IBGE, inactive)
    Downloaded via IPEA OData API, level Brasil, last updated 2016. Original old-PNAD survey, NOT harmonised with PNAD Continua (break at 2012; see PNADS_GINI series). Survey data only. No survey in 1980, 1991, 1994, 2000, 2010.
  • verified Income inequality (Gini, World Bank estimate) for Brazil, 1981-2024 (Gini index (0-100)) World Bank, SI.POV.GINI
    Downloaded via World Bank API 2026-11-01 (lastupdated 2026-10-08). Household survey per-capita income; gaps in years without survey. Not harmonised across the 2012 survey change; differs slightly from IPEA series.
  • verified Share of national income going to the top 1% (pre-tax), 2001-2024 (% of national income) World Inequality Database, Brazil, sptinc992j p99p100 (De Rosa, Flores & Morgan 2022; Flores & Zuniga-Cordero 2025)
    WID bulk file wid_all_data.zip (WID_data_BR.csv, downloaded 2026-11-01; WID updated 2026-10-30), variable sptinc992j (pre-tax national income, equal-split adults 20+). From 2001 combines household surveys, tax tabulations and national accounts (data_quality 3-4). Break: before 2001 WID uses a different modelled method. 2010 quality 2; 2024 quality 1 (provisional).
  • verified Share of national income going to the top 10% (pre-tax), 2001-2024 (% of national income) World Inequality Database, Brazil, sptinc992j p90p100
    WID bulk file wid_all_data.zip (WID_data_BR.csv, downloaded 2026-11-01; WID updated 2026-10-30), variable sptinc992j (pre-tax national income, equal-split adults 20+). Same method and breaks as the top-1% series.
  • unverified Share of national income going to the top 1% (pre-tax), WID modelled estimates, decade points 1920-1970 (% of national income) World Inequality Database, Brazil, sptinc992j p99p100 (Chancel & Piketty 2021 long-run paper; Chancel et al. 2023)
    WID bulk file wid_all_data.zip (WID_data_BR.csv, downloaded 2026-11-01; WID updated 2026-10-30), variable sptinc992j (pre-tax national income, equal-split adults 20+). Decade points only, data_quality 0 = modelled long-run estimate, not annual observed data. WID also holds 1980-2000 values but they are a constant placeholder (27.2%) and are NOT included. Break at 2001. Souza (2018) tax-data series (top 1% about 24% on average 1926-2015; 20-25% most of the time; WP167 pp.9-10) exists only as a chart, so it is not included.
  • unverified Share of national income going to the top 10% (pre-tax), WID modelled estimates, decade points 1920-1970 (% of national income) World Inequality Database, Brazil, sptinc992j p90p100
    WID bulk file wid_all_data.zip (WID_data_BR.csv, downloaded 2026-11-01; WID updated 2026-10-30), variable sptinc992j (pre-tax national income, equal-split adults 20+). Decade points only, data_quality 0 (modelled). 1980-2000 constant placeholder (58.6%) omitted. Break at 2001.
  • unverified Share of net personal wealth held by the top 10%, 1920-2024 (imputed) (% of net personal wealth) World Inequality Database, Brazil, shweal992j p90p100
    WID bulk file (downloaded 2026-11-01), variable shweal992j (net personal wealth, equal-split adults). All points data_quality 0 = imputed, not observed. WID metadata: 1800-1979 approximated by imputing a proxy (pweal) adjusted to the 1980 ratio; 1980-2025 from an external source. Decade points 1920-1970, annual from 1980. BREAK 1970->1980: the series steps down purely because the method changes (top 1%: 46.7 to 38.7), not a real fall.
  • verified Inequality of farmland among farms (Gini, 0-1), agricultural censuses 1975-2017 (Gini index (0-1)) Hoffmann, R., 'A distribuicao da posse de terra no Brasil (1985-2017)', Table 1 p.79, in Uma Jornada pelos Contrastes do Brasil (IPEA, 2020), from IBGE Censos Agropecuarios
    Read in the PDF (Table 1). Gini among establishments by area stratum; excludes landless families (including them: 0.911 in 2006, 0.902 in 2017). 1995 = census 1995-96. 2017 microdata (Table 6) gives 0.865. Other sources differ: Oxfam Brasil report Table 1 (IBGE) lists 0.857 (1985), 0.856 (1995), 0.872 (2006); a SciELO paper cites 0.866 for 2017. Censuses 1920-1970: no source found that I could open.
  • verified Labour share of GDP in Brazil, 1950-2023 (share of GDP (0-1)) Penn World Table 11.0 (Groningen Growth and Development Centre), variable labsh
    Downloaded the PWT 11.0 Excel file (dataverse.nl, file dated 2025-10-10), Brazil rows. Labour compensation share of GDP at current prices, adjusted by PWT for self-employed income; mixed national-accounts vintages, so revision breaks exist. Not an IBGE-published series.
  • verified V-Dem electoral democracy index, Brazil (index, 0 (low) to 1 (high)) Our World in Data grapher, from V-Dem (Varieties of Democracy) dataset
    Yearly values read from the OWID grapher CSV (Brazil rows), restricted to 1822-2025 (202 points). V-Dem is expert-coded with uncertainty bands that are not reproduced here. 1822 is the first year of the requested range, not necessarily V-Dem's first year (Brazil series start 1789 in the OWID file for the electoral, liberal and access indices).
  • verified Registered voters as % of population (IBGE-published) (% of total population) IBGE Estatisticas Historicas do Brasil, Tabela 13.2 'Populacao e proporcao do eleitorado inscrito'
    Percentages as printed in IBGE Table 13.2 for census years. 1950 printed as '22.05' (OCR-garbled, matches 11,455,149 / 51,944,397 = 22.05%). The 1980 value uses the 1982 electorate over the 1980 population, as IBGE's footnote states. Registered voters, not votes cast.
  • unverified Registered voters as % of population (derived and secondary) (% of total population) 1894: Agencia Senado 'Na primeira eleicao presidencial, ha 120 anos...'; 1989-2022: registered voters (Wikipedia/TSE) divided by World Bank SP.POP.TOTL
    1894 value 5.6% (about 800,000 eligible of 14.3 million) is as stated by the Agencia Senado article, read through a page summary; 351,000 votes were cast. 1989: 82,074,718 registered / World Bank population 146,502,972. 1994-2022: TSE electorate total / World Bank population (api.worldbank.org SP.POP.TOTL, last updated 2026-10-08). Derived by the research agent, so unverified. No sourced pre-1933 series other than 1894 was found.
  • verified Companies' direct share of candidate campaign receipts (% of candidate receipts) TSE open data, Prestacao de contas eleitorais, candidate receipts
    Candidate-level receipts only (ReceitaCandidato / ReceitasCandidatos files), nominal reais, not inflation-adjusted; committee and party-level accounts are NOT included. Direct corporate receipts divided by all candidate receipts (computed from the two series above, rounded to 0.01). Lower bound of corporate influence; see the note on transfers.
  • unverified Companies' direct share of candidate receipts, 2002 (heuristic) (% of candidate receipts) TSE open data, Prestacao de contas 2002, ReceitaCandidato.csv
    Candidate-level receipts only (ReceitaCandidato / ReceitasCandidatos files), nominal reais, not inflation-adjusted; committee and party-level accounts are NOT included. Corporate amount (CNPJ-length heuristic, see the 2002 corporate series) / total.

Investigations and their outcome
  • verified Convicted at first instance in Curitiba in 2017 (Guarujá triplex) and 2019 (Atibaia sítio); accused of receiving benefits from contractors.
    Outcome: ANNULLED. On 8 Mar 2021 STF Justice Edson Fachin annulled the Curitiba convictions for lack of jurisdiction of the 13th Federal Court of Curitiba; on 15 Apr 2021 the STF plenary upheld the annulment (8 votes to 3). On 23 Mar 2021 the STF Second Panel had found judge Sergio Moro partial in the triplex case. Not currently convicted on these cases. Sentence figures not verified. source
  • verified Accused in Lava Jato cases tried in Curitiba (Guaruja triplex, Atibaia farm, Instituto Lula headquarters and donations).
    Outcome: STF Justice Edson Fachin annulled the Curitiba decisions on 8 Mar 2021 (13th Federal Court lacked jurisdiction); the STF plenary upheld this by 8 votes to 3 on 15 Apr 2021, sending the cases to the Federal Court of the Federal District. Conviction nullified; guilt not decided. source

How political power is scored in every term

Every term gets the same six questions. The answers sit next to the money and inequality data, so patterns can be seen across 200 years.

QuestionWhat answers it here
1. Who ruled, and how did they get there?terms.json: ruler, title, how they came to power, how they left.
2. Who could choose them?Registered voters as % of population, nearest year to the term (IBGE census years, or derived values marked unverified).
3. Who backed them?Party or base from terms.json. Seats in Congress are missing for every term. Company campaign money (2002–2014) is on the timeline.
4. What checked them?V-Dem electoral democracy index at the start and end of the term.
5. What did they hand over?The cases that started in the term, with the decision-makers linked to each.
6. Who gained and who lost?Change in real minimum wage, Gini, SOE investment, public debt and V-Dem from start to end of the term.
Pattern, not proof. The scorecard shows what happened in the same years. It does not show why anyone acted, or that a decision caused a change in wages or inequality. An investigation is never shown as a fact: its outcome is printed exactly as in the data.

Rules used to build the page

  1. Case to term: a case belongs to the term in office in its start year. If several terms share that year, the term whose decision-makers are linked to the case wins (an "acted" link counts 2, "in office" counts 1). On a tie, the term in office on 1 July wins.
  2. People to term: the people files group people by term. Where one group covers several terms (Vargas 1930–1945, Floriano and Prudente), a person goes to each term their posts overlap. 3 people in no group are placed by the cases they are linked to. A person shows in every term they belong to; 9 people were in two era files and their records are merged.
  3. Indicator change: the start is the last full year before taking office (or the start year, if the term began after March). The end is the last year in office. If that year has no value, the nearest year within 2 years is used, and the years are printed. Start and end always come from the same series. Otherwise: "no data". The current term runs "to date".
  4. Gini and debt: the harmonised IPEA Gini is used first, then the old PNAD (0–1 scale), then the World Bank. Debt uses DLSP net debt, or before 1970 the gross federal internal debt. They are never mixed within one term.
  5. Both sides: verified ties whose kind is one of: board seat, client, client / buyer, client/board seat, consulting client / board chair (brief), education / former employer, employer after Central Bank, former consultant, former employer, former employer / client, former employer / co-founder, former subsidiary board, investor, later employer, lawyer/adviser (single source).
  6. Charts: series with different units have their own scale. Series the method notes say not to splice are drawn as separate marks: the four SOE counts, the two debt series, the three Gini series, the observed and modelled top shares, and Maddison against the World Bank (not drawn). Lines join only back-to-back years.

What data is missing

Most links between people and cases are "in office" only: 538 of 608 links. Only 70 name the person acting.

  • Seats in Congress: congress_share is empty in 52 of 52 terms.
  • 15 terms have no decision-makers mapped, mostly regencies, juntas and short interim terms.
  • Unverified entries: 42 of 296 posts and 222 of 608 case links.
  • State-company counts: only 12 years in four different counting bases (1980, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2003, 2006, 2010, 2011, 2016, 2017, 2021, 2022). Before 2000 there are just 1980, 1990 and 1995.
  • Privatization money: yearly figures cover 1991–2002 only. After 2002 there is just one federal total for 1990–2015.
  • Purchasing power: household income starts in 1995; the minimum wage starts in 1941; Maddison GDP per person ends in 2022.
  • Concentration: top income shares are observed only from 2001; earlier values are modelled decade points. Wealth shares are imputed for all years, with a method break between 1970 and 1980. Land Gini has 6 census points.
  • Labour share: the Penn World Table value is the same (0.5257) in every year from 1950 to 1992 in the file. The method note does not explain this, so treat that stretch with care.
  • Campaign money: only 2002–2014 elections, candidate accounts only, and company donations were banned after 2015.
  • Voters: no sourced share of voters before 1933 except one 1894 figure.
  • Colony: terms.json starts in 1822, so the crown years have no scorecard or indicator change.

Gaps the researchers reported

  • Anac presidents in order (Milton Zuanazzi, Denise Abreu, Solange Paiva Vieira, Marcelo Pacheco dos Guaranys, José Botelho de Queiroz) have no verified dates; not entered as person records.
  • Eletrobras presidents, Caixa president, Banco do Brasil before Bendine, MDA/Terra Legal ministers not mapped.
  • Cases e5-04, e5-05, e5-13 linked only to Lula; x-18 not linked; e5-18 and e5-23 link thinly.
  • Lula Lava Jato sentence details not verified; DOJ Petrobras 2018 settlement not confirmed.
  • Wikipedia pages were read in the first 100,000 characters only.
  • Round 7 ANP winners (e5-01) and Neoenergia/Vale as Norte Energia shareholders (e5-15) removed as unconfirmed on an opened page; Mantega post dates and Renato Duque end date not verified.
  • Role fields marked as inferred mean the person held the relevant post on the sale date per official lists; no opened page names them acting. Pages marked search-result were not fully opened. Wikipedia lists were used for post dates; where a page was truncated or absent, start/end are left null. Fact-checked 1 Nov 2026: statuses, basis and verified_sources added; unconfirmed accusations and counterparts removed.
  • Fact-checked 1 Nov 2026 against opened pages. status=verified means an opened source supports the entry; unverified entries are kept only for posts and case_links. basis: documented-act = an opened source names the person acting; in-office = held the post at the time.
